newsitem.title: USA: Bellwether sees fiscal 1998 net $0.45 shr.
newsitem.headline: Bellwether sees fiscal 1998 net $0.45 shr.

text.p: Bellwether Exploration Co said Monday it expects to report fiscal 1998 net earnings of $7 million, or $0.45 per share, as the sale of several properties causes production to decline by about 1,650 barrels of oil equivalent (BOE) per day.
The company said in a statement it sold certain non-core oil and natural gas properties for $17.3 million. The sales were effective June 30, when the company's fiscal year ended.
A Bellwether spokesman said the company expects to report fiscal 1997 fourth quarter and full year earnings in September.
The spokesman said the company expects fourth quarter earnings per share of $0.09 and $0.43 a share for the full fiscal year 1997.
For 1996 the company reported full-year EPS of $0.11. The company had 14.2 million shares outstanding in the fourth quarter and 9.1 million shares in 1996, the spokesman said.
The company said it estimates that due to the sale, its current production of 19,800 BOE per day will decline by approximately 1,650 BOE per day for fiscal year 1998.

The company said that based on the projected reduction and using an oil price of $20 per barrel and a natural gas price of $2.25 per thousand cubic feet (mcf), the company estimates that fiscal year 1998 cash flow will be approximately $49 million, or $3.25 per share.
Included in the sale are 117 of 179 fields originally purchased from partnerships and other entities managed by Torch Energy Advisors Inc in April 1997.
The properties include approximately 800 wells in 120 fields with estimated net reserves of 3.9 million barrels of oil equivalent.
As of March 31, 1997, the company's estimated net reserves were 40.1 million BOE.
